title: Zach Bryan Breaks Attendance Record at Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium While Wearing ‘Free Palestine’ Shirt for Second Night in a Row
description: Zach Bryan broke the attendance record at Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium on Saturday night, performing for 73,538 fans — the largest crowd for any
body:
Zach Bryan broke the attendance record at Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium on Saturday night, performing for 73,538 fans — the largest crowd for any event in the venue’s history — while wearing a “Free Palestine” shirt for the second night in a row.

	The move was a commentary on multiple levels, but most especially directed at Kraft, the billionaire owner of the Foxborough, Mass. stadium, who rallied fellow stadium owners to ban rapper Macklemore from his scheduled opening slot on the Ed Sheeran tour last month from performing at their venues. 
	

	The attendance record, which was broken on the second of Bryan’s two performances at the venue, was announced by tour promoter AEG on Sunday morning, and in a post on the stadium’s social media accounts. The latter announcement features photos of Bryan wearing the shirt, although the message is illegible and there was no mention of it in the post; however, it is referenced in the majority of the comments. Kraft used the Gilette Stadium account to defend his ban on Macklemore.


	The move was both a surprise — Bryan a proud Navy veteran working in the country genre, which has a fan base that would not be universally welcoming to such a purportedly left-wing position — and not, as Bryan has traditionally and steadfastly spoken his mind, from releasing a song critical of ICE raids to a bitter online dispute with country artist Gavin Adcock. According to fan footage, at least two of Bryan’s band members were wearing Palestine jerseys as well.

	Bryan was seen wearing a T-shirt (with the sleeves cut off, as is his nightly custom) bearing the logo “Free Palestine.” Beneath that on the shirt were an emblem of a pine tree and another message that read “An Appeal to Heaven.” These are references to a flag commissioned by George Washington in 1775 for a fleet of schooners sent to intercept British ships; later, it became the flag for the Massachusetts Navy — giving it a distinct historical and local connection for the Boston-area show.
	

	Bryan’s drummer, Nate Head bore a jersey with Palestine on the front and, on the back, the numeral 5 and the name “Hind Rajab.” Rajab was a 5-year-old girl in Gaza reported to have been killed by the Israeli military’s tank fire on Jan. 24, 2024, after having been trapped with her cousin and pleading for help in a disabled car for hours.

	Some news outlets ran with a widely spread and apparently false statement attributed to Bryan on Saturday. The statement, in which Bryan supposedly spoke up defending his stance from the night before, came from an X account that purports to belong to the singer but does not. (Bryan’s real X account has been deactivated for some time — it’s not clear for how long, since he had a history of saying contentious things, then deactivating, then restarting it.)

	Bryan’s politics have been somewhat elusive, with the singer-songwriter posting that he finds deep problems on both sides of America’s political divides. He previously raised the ire of some on the right with a song titled “Bad News,” which among its scattershot character-study lyrics, contained a seemingly negative reference to ICE (“ICE is gonna come, bust down your door / Try and build a house no one builds no more / But I got a telephone / Kids are all scared and all alone”). Following that, many on social media threatened to “Bud Light” him — that is, subject him to a boycott. But Bryan’s stadium shows have continued to be sellouts, and the artist has remained mostly apolitical as far as taking stands on any hot-button issues.

	The Foxborough shows are part of Bryan’s biggest tour yet, spanning more than 40 dates across North America and Europe starting in March 2026, and adds to a record-setting year for the artist. On September 27, 2025, he became the first artist ever to play Michigan Stadium, drawing 112,408 fans, the largest ticketed concert audience in U.S. history. That show surpassed the previous mark of 110,905, set by George Strait in Texas in 2024.

schema.headline: Zach Bryan Breaks Attendance Record at Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium While Wearing ‘Free Palestine’ Shirt for Second Night in a Row

title: Marjoe Gortner, Preacher and Actor Who Was Subject of Oscar-Winning Doc and Appeared in ‘Earthquake,’ ‘Falcon Crest,’ Dies at 82
description: Marjoe Gortner, whose childhood as an evangelical preacher was the subject of the Oscar-winning documentary “Marjoe” and who went on to have a caree
body:
Marjoe Gortner, whose childhood as an evangelical preacher was the subject of the Oscar-winning documentary “Marjoe” and who went on to have a career as an actor, died Friday. He was 82.

	His wife Susan Magestro told Variety he died in Santa Fe, N.M. Her memorial notice said he had been suffering from years of congestive heart failure. “Marjoe lived an extraordinary life, shaped by his imagination and rare gift for bringing people together,” the statement said.
	

	Actor Ian Ziering remembered him for his charity work, writing, “Marjoe Gortner was a force of nature. He became an evangelist in his teens, an actor in his young adulthood. His life story won an Oscar. I knew him because he produced the Marjoe Gortner celebrity sports invitationals that aired on CBS Saturdays for years. He brought celebrities all over the world to raise money for different charities …This man raised millions and millions of dollars for different charities while providing some of the most incredible celebrity experiences of my lifetime. I will never forget this man, and I will always be appreciative of not just what he did for me, but what he did for everyone who knew him.”


	Born in Long Beach, California, in an evangelical family, the name Marjoe is a combination of “Mary” and “Joseph.” His parents pushed him to become a child preacher, staging a photo op for the press when he performed a marriage ceremony at 4 years old. The family traveled around the country preaching and soliciting donations, and when Gortner was 16, his father absconded with what was reported to be $3 million in donations. 
	

	In his 20s, Gortner became disillusioned with the evangelical movement and became an aspiring actor in New York. 

	When he was approached by documentarians Howard Smith and Sarah Kernochan, he agreed to let them follow him around on his final revival tour in 1971, partially to help publicize his acting career. The resulting documentary, “Marjoe,” won the Oscar for best documentary. Roger Ebert saw it at the Cannes Film Festival and wrote “The real sleeper this year is ‘Marjoe. It generated the most electric response of anything at the festival.” It attracted considerable attention at the time, though it was later “lost” for many years until Kernochan was able to obtain rights to the film after tracking down the owner. 

	After making a record “Bad, but Not Evil,” he scored an acting role in the pilot for “Kojak.” Gortner went on to have roles as crazed drug dealers, outlaws, fake psychics and preachers in B movies and on television. In 1974’s “Earthquake,” he was the unhinged grocery store manager turned National Guardsman Sgt. Jody Joad. 

	He went on to appear in movies including Milton Katselas’ 1969 “When You Comin’ Back, Red Ryder?,” in which he played a troubled Vietnam veteran. The drama co-starred Candy Clark, to whom he was briefly married the year the film came out. 

	His other film appearances included “Viva Knieval,!” “Bobbie Joe and the Outlaw,” “The Survivalist,”  “Starcrash” and Walter Hill’s “Wild Bill.” During the ’70s and 1980s he appeared on TV series including “Police Story,” “Airwolf,” “T.J. Hooker,” “Street Hawk,” “Otherworld,” “The A Team,” “Fantasy Island” and “Falcon Crest,” as a corrupt psychic.

	His fifth wife, Susan Magestro, survives him.

schema.headline: Marjoe Gortner, Preacher and Actor Who Was Subject of Oscar-Winning Doc and Appeared in ‘Earthquake,’ ‘Falcon Crest,’ Dies at 82

	DIRECTV is making a play for sports fans just as the fall calendar hits its busiest stretch, rolling out a discount on its sports-focused streaming pack that bundles ESPN Unlimited Plan, NFL RedZone from NFL Network and dozens of other live sports channels.

	The streamer’s MySports Genre Pack is currently discounted to $49.99 for the first month, down from its regular $64.99 monthly price, for new customers. The package also comes with a five-day free trial and includes ESPN’s new Unlimited plan at no additional cost.
	

	The deal supports the pro football season that is now underway and the college football season as it heads into another packed month that will see dozens of games air across ABC and ESPN networks, including ranked teams and ranked-vs.-ranked matchups.


	In addition to ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU and ESPNews, MySports includes NFL Network, FS1, FS2, CBS Sports Network, Big Ten Network, SEC Network, NBA TV, NHL Network, MLB Network, TNT, TBS and truTV. Local ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC affiliates are also, though availability varies by location.

	NFL RedZone from NFL Network, of course, is designed for Sunday afternoons, jumping between games and showing scoring plays from across the league. It makes the add-on particularly useful for viewers who want to follow multiple teams without purchasing NFL Sunday Ticket. NFL Sunday Ticket itself is not included with DIRECTV and remains a separate subscription through YouTube and YouTube TV.

	The MySports deal extends well beyond football, too, arriving just in time for a packed fall sports calendar: Baseball’s postseason began on Sept. 29 with the Wild Card Series on NBC and Peacock, followed by the Division Series on Oct. 3, with the American League rounds airing on TBS and truTV and the National League rounds on Fox and FS1 before the World Series begins Oct. 23 on Fox. 
	

	The 2026-27 NHL season started in September, while the NBA regular season tips off Oct. 20, with ESPN beginning its coverage the following night with Timberwolves-Heat and Warriors-Lakers. TBS, truTV, FS1, ESPN, NBA TV and TNT are all included with MySports.

	Perhaps the biggest perk, though, is the ESPN Unlimited Plan, which is included with MySports rather than requiring another standalone subscription. The offering gives subscribers access to ESPN’s full suite of linear networks along with programming available through ESPN’s streaming service.

title: Box Office: ‘Digger’ Majorly Bombs With $8 Million Opening Weekend, ‘Verity’ Scores $32 Million Debut
description: In “Digger,” Tom Cruise portrays a powerful oil tycoon who is bracing for an ecological disaster of epic proportions. But nothing could have prepare
body:
In “Digger,” Tom Cruise portrays a powerful oil tycoon who is bracing for an ecological disaster of epic proportions. But nothing could have prepared him for the catastrophe that’s unfolding at the box office, where “Digger” has collapsed with an embarrassing $8 million from 3,321 North American theaters. Rivals believe the figure will be closer to $7.5 million when the final numbers are tallied on Monday.

	With a production budget of $160 to $180 million, “Digger” will wind up as not just one of the biggest bombs of the year but potentially of all time. Warner Bros. was hoping the combination of Tom Cruise, one of the biggest movie stars in the world, and director Alejandro González Iñárritu, whose critical and commercial wins include “Birdman” and “The Revenant,” would at least propel initial grosses to $18 million to $20 million. And even those ticket sales would have been financially disastrous for the mega-budgeted satirical film. Box office experts say a movie of this size would have needed a debut near $40 million to justify its price tag. Those projections were revised down (and revised down again) after a deluge of bad buzz. The R-rated satire opened in fifth place behind another newcomer, Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson’s psychological thriller “Verity,” and three holdovers, including “Resident Evil” and “Heart of the Beast.”
	

	“For a black comedy, the numbers are not bad. But black comedies are small films, and this isn’t a small film. It’s a Tom Cruise movie,” says analyst David A. Gross of Franchise Re. “The comedy walks a fine line, and when it misses, it misses.”
	

	Reviews and word-of-mouth for “Digger” have been so negative that Warner Bros. tried to embrace the unfavorable press. In a recent ad, the studio told moviegoers to “decide for yourself” after critics bashed the movie as “unpleasant” and “baffling.” Another marketing spot suggested that only American audiences disliked “Digger.” However the movie was equally rejected at the international box office with a tragic $12 million from 73 international markets for a global start of $20 million.

	“Digger” was always a gamble as the rare big-budget, star-driven R-rated original comedy. Warner Bros. greenlit the film for $125 million, but the price tag soared after production ran long. Since the studio spent another $100 million on global marketing efforts, “Digger” has a theatrical break-even point of roughly $350 million globally, according to executives with knowledge of similar films. A Warner Bros. spokesperson pushed back, saying the film’s break-even point is $300 million. Either way, “Digger” is primed to lose at least $150 million to $200 million theatrically. (Theater owners keep roughly half of ticket sales.) Profitability for the studio will take even longer because Cruise gets first-dollar gross, meaning he earns a percentage of revenues before the studio recoups any costs.

	“Even with respectable ancillary income based on the film’s pedigree,”  says Gross, referring to revenue streams like digital rental, sales, streaming and TV licensing, “the movie is going to lose a lot of money.”

	“Digger” extends a dismal year for Warner Bros. — having fielded such misfires as “The Bride” and “Supergirl” — and the timing was terrible. Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. is set to close next week. News broke on Friday that Warner co-chief’s Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy are leaving the studio when the merger closes on Oct. 6. The duo enjoyed a terrific box office run in 2025, with a stellar string of hits including “Sinners,” “A Minecraft Movie” and “Weapons.” But after pushing a number of big swings into 2026, not a single film has managed to cross $100 million domestically. 

	This time last year, few in Hollywood would have expected “Verity” to prevail over “Digger” at the domestic box office. Amazon MGM’s adaptation of Colleen Hoover’s best-seller has landed in first place with a solid $32.6 million from 3,510 theaters. It ranks as Hathaway’s third No. 1 opening of 2026 after this summer’s blockbusters  “The Devil Wears Prada 2″ and “The Odyssey.” A very pregnant Hathaway has recently joked that she’s now going to disappear for the rest of the year.
	

	“Verity” collected another $30 million at the international box office, bringing its worldwide tally to $62.5 million.

	Directed by “The Big Sick” filmmaker Michael Showalter, “Verity” centers around famed author Verity Crawford (Hathaway) who gets badly injured in a car accident, leaving her husband (Josh Hartnett) to hire a struggling writer (Johnson) to complete the remaining books in the popular series. Reviews and word-of-mouth has been negative; the film was saddled with a “C+” grade on CinemaScore and 34% on Rotten Tomatoes. However, “Verity” was produced for $40 million and is expected to turn a profit for Amazon MGM.

	“This is an excellent opening,” Gross says. “The reception is not hurting the film. Audiences are showing up in big numbers.”

	Hollywood has been eager to mine Hoover’s novels for the big screen because her work caters to an underserved female demographic, and the film adaptations carry modest production budgets, making them low-risk bets for studios. Opening weekend crowds for “Verity” were 78% female, while the largest age demo (38%) were between 25 and 34 years old. Among Hoover’s adaptations, “Verity” registers the second-biggest debut behind Sony’s 2024 sleeper hit “It Ends With Us” ($50 million) and ahead of Paramount’s 2025 film “Regretting You” (13.6 million) and Universal’s 2026 movie “Reminders of Him” ($17 million). “It Ends With Us” is the highest-grossing of the trio by far with $350 million globally.

	With general audiences rejecting “Digger,” Sony’s video game reboot “Resident Evil” remained in second place with $12.5 million in its third weekend of release. So far the R-rated movie, directed by “Weapons” filmmaker” Zach Cregger, has generated a strong $124.8 million domestically and $215 million globally against a $75 million budget.

	“Resident Evil” is the second consecutive box office win for Sony following “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which has now generated a staggering $954 million in North America and $2.5 billion globally. It’s the third-highest grossing movie in history behind “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.925 billion) and “Avatar” ($2.923 billion). Thanks to Disney’s recent re-release of “Avengers: Endgame,” which has collected a huge $126 million in two weekends, the Marvel behemoth once again ranks as the biggest release of all time. Disney reissued the blockbuster (with extra footage) to generate hype for “Avengers: Doomsday,” which lands on the big screen in December.
	

	Third place went to “Heart of the Beast” with $11 million in its sophomore outing, a 45% decline from its debut. So far, the Brad Pitt-led survival thriller has grossed $38.3 million in North America and $98.6 million worldwide and will imminently cross the $100 million mark. Since Paramount spent $82 million to produce the well-reviewed film, “Heart of the Beast” will rely on staying power and interest at the international box office to recoup in its theatrical run.

	“Primetime,” a psychological drama starring Robert Pattinson as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen, landed at No. 4 with $8 million in its second weekend. That’s a steeper 58% drop from its strong $19 million opening. So far, “Primetime” has amassed $34 million in North America against a modest $15 million budget. The movie, backed by A24, has yet to open in most international territories. 

	Through this weekend, the domestic box office stands at $7.95 billion, up 19% from the same point in 2025, according to Rentrak. Now the market is roughly $50 million away from crossing $8 billion — a milestone the industry didn’t cross last year until December. 

	“September certainly did its part,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian, referring to releases like “Resident Evil” and “Primetime.” “For a month that has often been viewed as something of a transitional period on the theatrical calendar, that is another strong indication of the depth and durability of the 2026 marketplace.”

schema.headline: Box Office: ‘Digger’ Majorly Bombs With $8 Million Opening Weekend, ‘Verity’ Scores $32 Million Debut

title: James Van Der Beek Was the ‘Soul’ of ‘Dawson’s Creek,’ Says Show Creator Kevin Williamson: ‘He Handled His Cancer With Such Grace and Courage’
description: “Dawson’s Creek” creator Kevin Williamson remembered the show’s late star Jame Van Der Beek on Saturday night while being honored with a Hero Award
body:
“Dawson’s Creek” creator Kevin Williamson remembered the show’s late star Jame Van Der Beek on Saturday night while being honored with a Hero Award at the Barbara Berlanti Heroes Gala, Greg Berlanti’s annual F Cancer benefit.

	Williams explained that the show, about a small-town high school student dreaming of becoming a Hollywood director, was inspired by his own life.

	“So when I was casting the role, I was basically looking for me, but I was looking for the good-looking, handsome, camera-ready, great jawline version of myself, someone people would actually want to see,” Williamson said, adding, “He became that person. James Van Der Beek gave voice to my childhood. He was the soul of the show.”
	

	Van Der Beek died in February, two years after being diagnosed with colorectal cancer in 2023.


	“I saw him go from a young kid to an extraordinary man, a husband, a father and a friend. James had a full character arc. He started out as a brat,” Williamson cracked. “He would get a script and he would call me, and he would be like, ‘Why do I have to say this word? Nobody knows what this word means.’ And I would say, ‘Well, don’t worry about it, the way you mumble nobody is going to hear it anyway.’ That was that was our relationship — Dawson talking to Dawson.”

	MORE: James Van Der Beek’s Career in Photos, From ‘Dawson’s Creek’ to ‘Pose’

	In September 2025, a “Dawson’s Creek” reunion was held in New York to raise funds for F Cancer and Van Der Beek’s treatment and support. Williamson, Michelle Williams, Katie Holmes, Joshua Jackson, Mary Beth Peil, John Wesley Shipp, Mary-Margaret Humes, Nina Repeta, Kerr Smith, Meredith Monroe and Busy Philipps took the stage at the Richard Rodgers Theater to read the 1998 pilot episode. Lin-Manuel Miranda stepped in for Van Der Beek because he was unable to attend due to illness.
	

	“Losing James earlier this year really knocked me over,” Williamson said, adding, “To lose the man who gave life to your own youth, I’m still unpacking that one. He handled his cancer with such grace and courage.”

	Williamson also talked about his mom, who died of lung cancer. “She was so outraged that Joey picked Pacey over Dawson,” he said. “I never heard the end of it.”

	The gala, held at the Santa Monica Barker Hangar, also honored “The Pitt” star Katherine LaNasa and the late NBA player Jason Collins.

title: ‘Avengers: Endgame’ Overtakes ‘Avatar’ as Highest-Grossing Movie in History With $2.925 Billion After ‘Encore’ Re-Release
description: “Avengers: Endgame” is once again the highest-grossing movie in box office history, reclaiming the title from “Avatar.” The two blockbusters have pa
body:
“Avengers: Endgame” is once again the highest-grossing movie in box office history, reclaiming the title from “Avatar.” The two blockbusters have passed the crown back and forth over the years as they’ve returned to theaters for various engagements.

	With Disney’s recent “Avengers: Endgame” theatrical re-release, the 2019 superhero epic has grossed $2.925 billion worldwide. That’s just above 2009’s “Avatar,” which has generated $2.923 billion globally after five re-releases.
	

	“Avatar” spent a decade as the biggest release ever until “Avengers: Endgame” overtook the record in 2019 during its initial run on the big screen. “Endgame” dropped to No. 2 on all-time charts in 2021 when “Avatar” returned to theaters in advance of 2021’s “Avatar: The Way of Water.” Five years later, and Earth’s Mightiest Heroes have triumphed over the Na’vi again.


	Disney is popping Champagne no matter which big-screen behemoth claims the No. 1 spot. “Avatar” was released by 20th Century Fox, which Disney now owns after the companies merged in 2019. With Fox’s film assets, Disney is responsible for seven of the 10 highest grossing movies, including “”Avatar: The Way of Water” ($2.33 billion), “Titanic” ($2.26 billion) and “Avengers: Infinity War” ($2.05 billion).

	Disney and Marvel reissued “Avengers: Endgame” to generate excitement for “Avengers: Doomsday,” which debuts in December. “Avengers: Endgame” was notable as the culmination of 21 movies (many of them blockbusters in their own right) over 10 years and brought together just about every comic book star, from Robert Downey Jr. (Iron Man), Chris Evans (Captain America) and Scarlett Johansson (Black Widow) to Tom Holland (Spider-Man), Chadwick Boseman (Black Panther) and Anthony Mackie (Falcon). 
	

	Marvel, after an uneven post-pandemic stretch, is reuniting nearly every superhero in the galaxy in “Doomsday” for the first time since “Endgame.” The re-release of “Endgame” has generated more than $126 million worldwide — and the turnout has theater owners buzzing for “Doomsday,” which is expected to be one of the year’s biggest movies. Anthony and Joe Russo returned to direct “Avengers: Doomsday,” the 39th installment in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The MCU has long been the most commercially successful film franchise in history. After this summer’s juggernaut “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” climbed to $2.5 billion and counting, the sprawling property has generated a combined $35.07 billion across all movies.

schema.headline: ‘Avengers: Endgame’ Overtakes ‘Avatar’ as Highest-Grossing Movie in History With $2.925 Billion After ‘Encore’ Re-Release

title: Pete Hegseth Chugs ‘Spider-Man’s Non-Alcoholic B—- Beer’ in ‘SNL’ Cold Open That Mocks Tom Holland, Mitch McConnell and JD Vance
description: In the Oct. 3 cold open on “Saturday Night Live,” Andrew Dismukes and Ashley Padilla play Republican strategists who have their work cut out for the
body:
In the Oct. 3 cold open on “Saturday Night Live,” Andrew Dismukes and Ashley Padilla play Republican strategists who have their work cut out for them building buzz for their party.

	Marcello Hernández comes in first as Marco Rubio, who speaks to constituents in Spanish, admits that Trump did not live up to expectations and his endless war is not making things better.

	Mikey Day then shows up as a frozen Mitch McConnell in a wheelchair, only able to give the peace sign and nearly derailing the fourth wall of the sketch when he mistakenly tries to say “Live from New York” too early.
	

	Vice President JD Vance stopped by, played by Jeremy Culhane, and his lack of charisma was mocked when he started his camera test by saying, “Hi, I’m JD Vance,” before getting dismissed.


	The sketch’s highlight was Colin Jost returning as Pete Hegseth, who immediately chugs one of Tom Holland’s Bero beers, which he refers to as “Spider-Man’s new non-alcoholic bitch beer.”

	The sketch, which parodied his unhinged “State of the Force” address this week, he also urges Republicans to do something shocking: “I need all you patriots at home to do the gayest thing ever and vote.”

	He also noted that, “I’m putting God back in war and it’s working. Our soldiers are praying a lot more than they used to.”

	Trump, played by James Austin Johnson, also dropped by, saying, “Let me cook.”

	He also made fun of his real-life strategy to reimburse American voters for a Republican midterm win, saying, “If the Republicans win, I’ll give everyone $5,000 and that is not a bribe because I have no intention of following through on that promise.”
	

	The episode’s host is Dakota Johnson and the musical guest is Turnstile.

title: Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, Indian Filmmaker Behind ‘Pushpaka Vimana,’ ‘Michael Madana Kama Rajan’ and ‘Aditya 369’ Dies at 95
description: Revered Indian filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, whose work spanned the 1957 Telugu-language classic “Mayabazar” and this year’s musical “Sing Gee
body:
Revered Indian filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, whose work spanned the 1957 Telugu-language classic “Mayabazar” and this year’s musical “Sing Geetham,” died Oct. 3 in Chennai following a period of ill health. He was 95.

	Rao made some 60 features in the Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and Hindi languages, and moved between farce, fantasy, mythology and science fiction. He also composed music for some of his films and took occasional acting roles.
	

	“Sing Geetham,” in which the cast sings rather than speaks, reached cinemas in June this year. It was his first film as director in a decade.


	Rao trained under director K.V. Reddy, assisting on “Mayabazar” (1957) and “Jagadeka Veeruni Katha” (1961). He stepped behind the camera himself in 1972 with the Telugu drama “Neethi Nijayithi.” His Tamil film “Dikkatra Parvathi” (1974) took the Indian National Film Award for best Tamil feature.

	Rao’s partnership with the actor Kamal Haasan began with the 1979 Telugu comedy “Sommokadidhi Sokokadidhi,” in which Haasan played two parts, and continued with “Raja Paarvai” (1981), Haasan’s 100th film and his first as producer. “Pushpaka Vimana” (1987) came next. Rao wrote and co-produced the comedy, and nobody in it utters a line. Haasan plays a broke graduate who passes himself off as a rich man at a hotel, with Amala Akkineni co-starring. Because there was no dialogue to translate, actors could be drawn from across India, and the film went on to win the Indian National Film Award for best popular film providing wholesome entertainment.

	Their Tamil run continued with “Apoorva Sagodharargal” (1989), where Haasan took three roles, among them a circus performer with dwarfism, and Indian comedy classic “Michael Madana Kama Rajan” (1990), where Haasan had four roles. They reteamed on “Magalir Mattum” and, in 2005, “Mumbai Xpress.”
	

	That Tamil turn followed Rao’s long stint in Kannada with Rajkumar. The star led seven Rao films, beginning with “Haalu Jenu” in 1982, and four of those were later redone in Telugu. In 1988, Rajkumar announced that he planned to step away from acting for a while, and that steered the director toward Tamil projects.

	At home in Telugu, Rao cast dancer Sudha Chandran in “Mayuri” (1985), a dramatization of her own comeback after losing a leg. It collected 14 Nandi Awards, the state honors of Andhra Pradesh, a record haul. With Nandamuri Balakrishna he made “Aditya 369” (1991), a time-travel adventure, and the folklore fantasy “Bhairava Dweepam” (1994), which earned Rao the Nandi for best director.

	The Film Federation of India presented him with its Life Achievement Award in 2011. He also picked up three Karnataka State Film Awards.

title: Cornell Jane Doe Attorney Claims Evidence May Have Been Dumped in Lake, More Videos Exist
description:
Jane Doe Attorney
                          Evidence May Have Been Dumped In Lake
body:
Jane Doe Attorney
                          Evidence May Have Been Dumped In Lake
                          ... More Videos, Pics Exist
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 4, 2026
                            7:06 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The attorney representing the Jane Doe accusing 7 members of the Chi Phi fraternity at Cornell University of drugging and sexually assaulting her is claiming that evidence could have been dumped in a lake for all he knows ... and that there's more video and pics of the alleged gang rape.
      
    
            Sitting down with CNN's Jake Tapper Sunday ... lawyer Thomas Giuffra raised concerns that crucial evidence -- including additional videos and photos -- was lost because a search warrant was never executed by authorities.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Giuffra said ... "They would have grabbed every single one of these phones of these guys. They would have downloaded all this material. I'm confident, knowing this day and age and the group that we're dealing with, that there were other photos, there were videos."
      

            Jane Doe's lawyer added that he believes these videos are presently at the "bottom of Lake Cayuga."
      
    
            He alleged ... "Once they knew there was a problem, they cleared everything out and they got rid of it."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As for Jane Doe ... he said she's received several threats by people wanting her to drop the lawsuit ... and called her harassers "disgusting."
      
    
            We reported earlier ... Giuffra previously said that his client "is not doing well" and was "under siege on social media, where people are trying to identify her."

            Ed Sheeran is getting some musical support after his opening acts quit his tour ... as the singer brought out The Fray's former lead singer Isaac Slade.
      
    
          Waiting for your permission to load TikTok Post.
      
    
            Isaac -- who left The Fray in 2022 to focus on his mental health -- performed songs like "How to Save a Life" and "You Found Me" before Ed came out on his Saturday night show in Atlanta.
      
    
            The opener also referenced the ongoing conflict in Gaza.
      

          Waiting for your permission to load TikTok Post.
      
    
            Isaac said ... "Everybody seems to be taking sides in this world and that’s good. What’s happening over there is wrong but if we’re going to get through it, we’re going to need people to step into that middle place, that common ground."
      
    
            We reported earlier ... all of Ed's opening acts pulled out of his tour after rapper Macklemore was ousted over pro-Palestine comments he made at a pair of shows in New Jersey.
      
    
            Ed eventually addressed the controversy at his show in Philly last month ... saying that he was "appalled" by the ongoing Israel-Palestine conflict ... and apologized to fans.
      
    
            The "Shape of You" singer's 2 shows at Robert Kraft's Gillette Stadium were canceled last weekend.
      
    
            As for Macklemore ... he recently revealed that his standalone "Free Palestine" tour just sold out all of its tickets across 3 performances.
